atoms.text: Despite the Romans leaving Britain over 1,600 years ago, they have still made a big impact on these isles. The Romans laid the foundations of many of the major cities in the UK today, including London. They also built an extensive network of roads, popularised coins and introduced sewage systems.

As the Romans built roads across Britain, they measured distances using the Roman mile. This measurement came from the Latin phrase mille passus, meaning “a thousand paces”. Over time, it was standardised to become the modern mile used in the UK today.
They would have measured these distances using their numbering system: Roman numerals. These are no longer part of everyday life but can still be seen on some clocks, monuments and buildings.
